We need to find the maximum possible beauty: after each index can be changed at most once to any value within [nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k], we want the maximum possible length of a subsequence consisting of equal elements.

Observation: Since we can change each element arbitrarily within its allowed interval, the problem reduces to: we want to find a value X such that as many indices i as possible have X within [nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k]; we can then set those elements to X (by possibly modifying them if needed) to get a subsequence of all X's. Since we can choose any subsequence (preserving order), we can always take all indices i where X is feasible (since we can keep them in order). So the maximum beauty equals the maximum number of indices i for which there exists a common value X that lies in all of their intervals [nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k]. In other words, we want the maximum size of a subset of intervals that have a non-empty intersection.

This is a classic problem: given intervals, find the maximum number of intervals that overlap at a point. Equivalent to: find the point with maximum coverage.

Since each interval is [nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k]. We can compute all interval endpoints and do a sweep line: sort events (start, +1), (end+epsilon, -1) but since intervals are inclusive, we can treat end as +1 after the point. Simpler: sort all start points and end points; use two pointers or sort events.

Given constraints up to 1e5, O(n log n) is fine.

Alternatively, we can sort nums and then use sliding window: because intervals are centered at nums[i] with radius k. If we sort the original nums, then for a given i as left pointer, we can find the furthest j such that nums[j] - nums[i] <= 2*k (since intervals [nums[i]-k, nums[i]+k] and [nums[j]-k, nums[j]+k] intersect iff the distance between centers <= 2k). Actually, condition for intersection of two intervals: max(left_i, left_j) <= min(right_i, right_j). left = nums[i]-k, right = nums[i]+k. Intersection non-empty iff nums[i]-k <= nums[j]+k and nums[j]-k <= nums[i]+k which simplifies to |
